title: The Chamber Where Epochs Rest Without Ending

features.name: the spiral wherein time pools
features.desc-on-touch: You feel the stone worn smooth by epochs that forgot to leave. Each spiral is a year that decided to rest instead of fall.

features.name: the pool that asks nothing
features.desc-on-touch: The water has stopped reflecting. It shows you only its own depth, and that depth is exactly as deep as you've lived.

features.name: the bell-stone
features.desc-on-touch: A stone carved into the shape of a bell, ringing at a frequency too low to hear. You feel it in your bones. It has been ringing since before you arrived.

features.name: the circle of kept bones
features.desc-on-touch: Arranged in a perfect ring: the skeleton of patience. Each bone a moment that chose to become weight instead of motion. You can read their names in how they're placed.

features.name: the standing count
features.desc-on-touch: Numbers carved so deep the stone has started to argue with them. Each digit is a year. None of them add up the same way twice.

inscription: only rest that ends never truly rested

file.name: Epochs_Recorded_Then_Forgotten.mp3
file.note: A long humming tone at descending frequencies, each note a century fading into the next. Corruption: the timestamps rearrange. Oldest epochs play first, newest last; then the order reverses.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the chamber where water forgets its hurry
narr: You sit by the pool, and she sits beside you, both of you
still. The water is telling you something in a language older
than speaking. She reaches down and touches the surface—not
to break it, but to listen. The pool hums back at her. You
understand then: this is where epochs come when they're too
tired to sing. She nods. You both stay until the sun moves on.

exits.label: back up, where the singing still rises
